newsitem.title: MEXICO: Two Mexican pop stars marry on TV -- with sponsors.
newsitem.headline: Two Mexican pop stars marry on TV -- with sponsors.

text.p: The "Marriage of the Year" of Mexican pop stars Lucero and Manuel Mijares on television late Saturday brought some $12 million in advertising revenue to the network Televisa, newspapers reported Sunday.
The three-hour ceremony was broadcast live in Mexico, the United States and elsewhere in Latin America.

Televisa reportedly paid the couple $7 million for exclusive rights. Mexican newspapers were forced to take their photographs from the TV screen of the 27-year-old bride, and her bridegroom, Mijares, 38.
Televisa officials denied the $7 million price tag, saying that Televisa broadcast the service simply because of the "great love" in Mexico for the bride and groom.

Fans who flocked to the grand colonial house, El Colegio de la Paz de las Vizcainas, in the city centre to catch a glimpse of the bride -- known as "The Girlfriend of America" -- were kept firmly out of view.
Traffic was blocked; hundreds of policemen were taken off the beat to keep onlookers back, and the 1,000 guests invited were almost all from the nation's pop and political elite.
They were married by Mexico's Archbishop Norberto Rivera, who urged them to "Work on behalf on the most needy", and Pope John Paul II sent a personal special blessing.
